title: Indian Penal Code 1860
note: IPC has been replaced by Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 effective 1 July 2024. IPC sections remain relevant for offences committed before that date.

sections.title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
sections.description: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone.
sections.punishment: Same as the principal offence
sections.example: A and B together attack C with the common intention to kill him. Both are liable under the main offence read with Section 34 IPC.

sections.title: Abetment of a thing
sections.description: A person abets the doing of a thing who: firstly, instigates any person to do that thing; or secondly, engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing, if an act or illegal omission takes place in pursuance of that conspiracy; or thirdly, intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
sections.punishment: Same as the principal offence unless otherwise specified
sections.example: A instigates B to kill C. Even if B does not kill C, A may be guilty of abetment.

sections.title: Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
sections.description: Whoever abets any offence shall, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.
sections.punishment: Same as principal offence
sections.example: A abets B to commit theft; B commits theft. A is punished under Section 109 read with Section 379.

sections.title: Punishment of criminal conspiracy
sections.description: Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence. Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Same as abetment of offence (for serious offences); up to 6 months / fine for others
sections.example: A, B and C agree to murder D. All three are guilty of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B.

sections.title: Punishment for rioting
sections.description: Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A mob of 10 people gathers and begins attacking a shop. All members are liable for rioting under Section 147.

sections.title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
sections.description: Whoever is guilty of rioting, being armed with a deadly weapon or with anything which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: Members of a mob carrying iron rods and knives attack a person. Those armed are liable under Section 148.

sections.title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
sections.description: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence.
sections.punishment: Same as the principal offence
sections.example: Five people form an unlawful assembly to burn a house; one member burns it — all five are liable under Section 149.

sections.title: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc.
sections.description: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote, on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community or any other ground whatsoever, disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both; up to 5 years if committed in place of worship
sections.example: A person delivers a speech inciting hatred between two religious communities. He is liable under Section 153A.

sections.title: Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions
sections.description: Whoever voluntarily obstructs any public servant in the discharge of his public functions, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 months imprisonment or fine up to ₹500 or both
sections.example: A refuses to let a police officer conduct a lawful search and physically blocks him. A is liable under Section 186.

sections.title: Obscene acts and songs
sections.description: Whoever, to the annoyance of others does any obscene act in any public place, or sings, recites or utters any obscene song, ballad or words, in or near any public place, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 months imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A performs an obscene act on a public street causing annoyance to passersby. A is liable under Section 294.

sections.title: Punishment for murder
sections.description: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Death or life imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A kills B with the intention to cause death. A is liable under Section 302 IPC.

sections.title: Causing death by negligence
sections.description: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A driver runs over a pedestrian due to rash and negligent driving. He is liable under Section 304A.

sections.title: Dowry death
sections.description: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs under abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death', and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
sections.punishment: Minimum 7 years; may extend to life imprisonment
sections.example: A woman is burnt to death within 3 years of marriage after repeated demands for dowry. Her husband is liable under Section 304B.

sections.title: Abetment of suicide
sections.description: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Up to 10 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A continuously harasses B until B commits suicide. A is liable under Section 306.

sections.title: Attempt to murder
sections.description: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned.
sections.punishment: Up to 10 years + fine; life imprisonment if hurt caused
sections.example: A fires a gun at B intending to kill him but B survives. A is liable under Section 307.

sections.title: Attempt to commit suicide
sections.description: Whoever attempts to commit suicide and does any act towards the commission of such offence, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. (Note: Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 effectively decriminalizes attempt to suicide by presuming the person to be under severe stress.)
sections.punishment: Up to 1 year simple imprisonment or fine or both (rarely enforced; see Mental Healthcare Act 2017)
sections.example: A attempts to kill himself by consuming poison but survives. Technically liable under Section 309, but treated as a mental health issue under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017.

sections.title: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt
sections.description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 1 year imprisonment or fine up to ₹1,000 or both
sections.example: A punches B causing pain and minor injury. A is liable under Section 323.

sections.title: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means
sections.description: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death, or by means of fire or any heated substance, or by means of any poison or any corrosive substance, or by means of any explosive substance or by means of any substance which it is deleterious to the human body to inhale, to swallow, or to receive into the blood, or by means of any animal, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A cuts B with a knife causing injury. A is liable under Section 324.

sections.title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
sections.description: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Minimum 1 year up to 5 years imprisonment + fine (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013)
sections.example: A grabs or touches B (a woman) inappropriately without her consent. A is liable under Section 354.

sections.title: Punishment for kidnapping
sections.description: Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Up to 7 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A takes a 10-year-old child without the consent of the child's guardian. A is liable under Section 363.

sections.title: Kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage
sections.description: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any woman with intent that she may be compelled, or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry any person against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, or knowing it to be likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Up to 10 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A kidnaps B (a woman) to force her into marriage. A is liable under Section 366.

sections.title: Punishment for rape
sections.description: Whoever, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), commits rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Aggravated forms (sub-section 2) attract minimum 10 years to life or death in some cases.
sections.punishment: Minimum 10 years rigorous imprisonment to life imprisonment + fine; death penalty in repeat offences or rape of child under 12
sections.example: A commits non-consensual sexual intercourse with B. A is liable under Section 376 IPC.

sections.title: Intercourse by a person in authority
sections.description: Whoever, being in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship, or a public servant, or superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law, or a hospital, and commits rape on a woman in such institution or within its premises, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Minimum 10 years rigorous imprisonment to life imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A police officer rapes a woman in custody. He is liable under Section 376A.

sections.title: Unnatural offences
sections.description: Whoever voluntarily has carnal intercourse against the order of nature with any man, woman or animal, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. (Note: The Supreme Court in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018) read down this section to decriminalise consensual same-sex relations between adults.)
sections.punishment: Up to life imprisonment or up to 10 years + fine (non-consensual acts; consensual adult same-sex acts decriminalised per SC 2018)
sections.example: A commits non-consensual carnal intercourse against the order of nature with B. A is liable under Section 377.

sections.title: Punishment for theft
sections.description: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A picks B's wallet from B's pocket without consent. A is liable under Section 379.

sections.title: Theft in dwelling house
sections.description: Whoever commits theft in any building, tent or vessel, which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or used for the custody of property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Up to 7 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A breaks into B's house and steals jewellery. A is liable under Section 380.

sections.title: Punishment for robbery
sections.description: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.
sections.punishment: Up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment + fine; up to 14 years if on highway between sunset and sunrise
sections.example: A snatches B's bag while threatening B with violence. A is liable under Section 392.

sections.title: Punishment for dacoity
sections.description: Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Life imprisonment or up to 10 years rigorous imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A gang of six persons robs a bank using weapons. All are liable under Section 395.

sections.title: Robbery, or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt
sections.description: If, at the time of committing robbery or dacoity, the offender uses any deadly weapon, or causes grievous hurt to any person, or attempts to cause death or grievous hurt to any person, the imprisonment with which such offender shall be punished shall not be less than seven years.
sections.punishment: Minimum 7 years rigorous imprisonment
sections.example: A shoots at B while robbing him, causing grievous injury. A is liable under Section 397 with minimum 7 years imprisonment.

sections.title: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
sections.description: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A is entrusted with B's money and dishonestly misappropriates it. A is liable under Section 406.

sections.title: Criminal breach of trust by public servant, or by banker, merchant or agent
sections.description: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property in his capacity of a public servant or in the way of his business as a banker, merchant, factor, broker, attorney or agent, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Life imprisonment or up to 10 years imprisonment + fine
keywords: breach of trust by public servant
sections.example: A government officer misappropriates public funds entrusted to him. He is liable under Section 409.

sections.title: Dishonestly receiving stolen property
sections.description: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A buys a mobile phone from B knowing B had stolen it. A is liable under Section 411.

sections.title: Cheating
sections.description: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, or intentionally induces the person so deceived to do or omit to do anything which he would not do or omit if he were not so deceived, and which act or omission causes or is likely to cause damage or harm to that person in body, mind, reputation or property, is said to 'cheat'.
sections.punishment: Defined in Section 417 (up to 1 year or fine or both) and Section 420 (up to 7 years + fine)
sections.example: A deceives B by falsely claiming to be a bank officer and induces B to hand over money. A has 'cheated' within the meaning of Section 415.

sections.title: Punishment for cheating
sections.description: Whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 1 year imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A cheats B by delivering adulterated goods. A is liable for simple cheating under Section 417.

sections.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
sections.description: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Up to 7 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A poses as a government official and collects money from B promising a government contract. A is liable under Section 420.

sections.title: Punishment for criminal trespass
sections.description: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 months imprisonment or fine up to ₹500 or both
sections.example: A enters B's farm without permission with intent to intimidate B. A is liable under Section 447.

sections.title: Punishment for house-trespass
sections.description: Whoever commits house-trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 1 year imprisonment or fine up to ₹1,000 or both
sections.example: A enters B's home without consent or authority. A is liable under Section 448.

sections.title: Forgery for purpose of cheating
sections.description: Whoever commits forgery, intending that the document or electronic record forged shall be used for the purpose of cheating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.punishment: Up to 7 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: A forges B's signature on a cheque to withdraw money from B's account. A is liable under Section 468.

sections.title: Using as genuine a forged document or electronic record
sections.description: Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly uses as genuine any document or electronic record which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged document or electronic record, shall be punished in the same manner as if he had forged such document or electronic record.
sections.punishment: Same as Section 463 (forgery) — up to 2 years / fine; or up to 7 years + fine if forged for cheating (Section 468)
sections.example: A uses a forged degree certificate to get a job, knowing it is fake. A is liable under Section 471.

sections.title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
sections.description: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 'Cruelty' means (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical); or (b) harassment with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security.
sections.punishment: Up to 3 years imprisonment + fine
sections.example: B's husband and in-laws repeatedly harass her for more dowry and physically assault her. The husband and relatives are liable under Section 498A.

sections.title: Punishment for defamation
sections.description: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years simple imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A publishes a false statement that B is a thief, harming B's reputation. A is liable under Section 500.

sections.title: Intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace
sections.description: Whoever intentionally insults, and thereby gives provocation to any person, intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause him to break the public peace, or to commit any other offence, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years imprisonment or fine or both
sections.example: A insults B in a public place with the intention of provoking B to commit a breach of peace. A is liable under Section 504.

sections.title: Punishment for criminal intimidation
sections.description: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and if the threat be to cause death or grievous hurt, or to cause the destruction of any property by fire, or to cause an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or to impute unchastity to a woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment: Up to 2 years imprisonment or fine or both; up to 7 years if threat involves death, grievous hurt or imputing unchastity to a woman
sections.example: A threatens to kill B if B does not hand over money. A is liable under Section 506.
